correctness.rationale: For every integer d>=3, exact-length cube walks characterize alternating supports. The Hamming-distance-to-support parity maxima differ by exactly one, implying the entrance clock R(S)-1. Singletone supports contribute the maximal shell; overlapping d-neighbor stars contribute the penultimate shell with the pair correction. A factorial-moment argument bounds exceptional neighborhood-overlap tuples and proves Poisson(e^{-2a}); a radius-two predecessor union bound proves second-step consensus. Independent exhaustive state, covering-radius, and bit-parallel moment/sampling programs passed. Finite computations corroborate but do not supply the universal proof.

value.rationale: The critical one-step fixation probability exp(-exp(-2a)) is a nondegenerate Gumbel transition at initial density 1/2 on a canonical high-dimensional graph; the second update almost surely finishes consensus despite the sharp d-1 exceptional transient. Exact two-terminal-shell formulas identify the geometric rare exceptions using antipodes, overlapping Hamming-neighborhood stars and a nontrivial pair correction. This is a natural structural and stochastic gap, not arbitrary numerical slicing.
